title: Kladdkaka
subtitle: Swedish sticky chocolate cake
excerpt: A rich, fudgy chocolate cake that is deliberately underbaked to give a sticky, almost molten centre. Kladdkaka means 'sticky cake' in Swedish and it is one of Sweden's most popular cafe cakes. The centre should wobble when you take it from the oven.
sourceNotes: Kladdkaka means 'sticky cake' in Swedish. It is intentionally underbaked to give a fudgy, almost molten-centred texture. It is one of Sweden's most popular cakes -- sold in every cafe and bakery.

content.text: Kladdkaka is one of the easiest cakes to make badly by leaving it in the oven too long. The centre must wobble when you shake the tin. It firms up as it cools. If it is fully set when you take it out, it is overdone.

items.prepNote: use 4 tbsp cocoa powder instead for a cleaner chocolate flavour

content.text: Heat oven to 175°C. Grease a 23cm springform tin and line the base with baking paper.
Whisk melted butter and sugar together until combined. Beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, treacle or cocoa, vanilla, and salt until just combined.
Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 18-20 minutes. The edges should be set but the centre should wobble noticeably when you shake the tin.
Cool completely in the tin before removing. Dust with icing sugar to serve.

items.symptom: Cake is completely set with no sticky centre
items.cause: Oven too hot or baked too long
items.fix: This cake should wobble in the middle when you shake the tin. Pull it out earlier next time -- it sets further as it cools.

content.text: Sweden. Every Swedish cafe has it. Eaten at fika (the Swedish coffee break). The deliberate underbaking is the whole point -- a fully set kladdkaka is considered a failure. Serve in small slices as it is very rich.
